items.title: CANVAS 2025 in Salt Lake City
items.summary: At the ASA-CSSA-SSSA Annual Meeting I presented our minimum interpretable predictor set for scalable soil health assessment, moderated Session 202 on soil carbon farming as a climate solution, and judged the student oral competition. Between sessions, a trip to the Great Salt Lake, a terminal lake where water, salt, and land meet.

facts.text: The largest saline lake in the Western Hemisphere, and a shorebird site of hemispheric importance.
A terminal lake: water leaves only by evaporation, with no outlet to the sea.
A railroad causeway built in 1959 splits the lake into Gunnison Bay to the north and Gilbert Bay to the south.
The north arm runs about 26 to 30% salinity against 12 to 15% in the south, and salt-loving microbes tint it purple-pink.
Typically 3 to 5 times saltier than the ocean, too salty for fish, and an important source of brine shrimp.
